classes.desc: subqueries in FROM, WHERE and SELECT, lined up after their "("

cases.name: IN subquery
cases.sql: select * from users where id in (select user_id from orders where amount > 100)

cases.name: NOT IN subquery with AND inside
cases.sql: select * from users where id not in (select user_id from orders where status = 'refunded' and amount > 100)

cases.name: scalar subquery in comparison
cases.sql: select id, amount from orders where amount > (select avg(amount) from orders)

cases.name: correlated EXISTS
cases.sql: select u.id from users u where exists (select 1 from orders o where o.user_id = u.id)

cases.name: AND NOT EXISTS
cases.sql: select u.id from users u where u.active = 1 and not exists (select 1 from orders o where o.user_id = u.id)

cases.name: derived table in FROM
cases.sql: select t.user_id, t.total from (select user_id, sum(amount) as total from orders group by user_id) t where t.total > 1000

cases.name: derived table with AS alias
cases.sql: select * from (select id from users where active = 1) as active_users

cases.name: scalar subquery in SELECT
cases.sql: select u.id, (select count(*) from orders o where o.user_id = u.id) as order_count from users u

cases.name: subquery in HAVING
cases.sql: select user_id, count(*) as n from orders group by user_id having count(*) > (select avg(cnt) from order_counts)

cases.name: nested subqueries
cases.sql: select * from users where id in (select user_id from orders where product_id in (select id from products where price > 100))

cases.name: subquery as function argument, inside parentheses
cases.sql: select coalesce((select max(x) from t), 0) as m from u
